Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The real coordinate space (of dimension [MATH: n]) is the set of all possible column vectors of height [MATH: n,] whose components are real numbers. Symbolically, we represent the real coordinate space of dimension [MATH: n] as [MATH: \mathbb{R}^n.]

Content:
For example, the following vectors are in [MATH: \mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R}^2,] [MATH: \mathbb{R}^3,] and [MATH: \mathbb{R}^5,] respectively:

Content:
[MATH: [sqrt(4); 0]]

Content:
We've already encountered several operations on vectors in [MATH: \mathbb{R}^2] or [MATH: \mathbb{R}^3,] namely, vector addition and subtraction, scalar multiplication, and the dot product. All of these operations work the same way in [MATH: \mathbb{R}^n.]

---

Item 2 — Example: Calculating a Multiple of a Vector

Example Prompt:
Let [MATH: [− 4; 6; 3; 0]] Find [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2} \mathbf{a}.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Multiplying each component of [MATH: \mathbf{a}] by [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2},] we get

[MATH: (1)/(2)a|= (1)/(2)[− 4; 6; 3; 0]; = [(1)/(2) ⋅ (− 4); (1)/(2) ⋅ 6; (1)/(2) ⋅ 3; (1)/(2) ⋅ 0]; = [− 2; 3; (3)/(2); 0].]

Item 5 — Tutorial: Adding Two Vectors

Content:
To add two vectors in [MATH: \mathbb{R}^n,] we just need to add their corresponding components. To illustrate, consider the vectors [MATH: \mathbf{a},\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{R}^4,] given by

Content:
[MATH: [5; 1; − 3; 6]]

Content:
To compute [MATH: \mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b},] all we have to do is to add each component of the vector [MATH: \mathbf{a}] with the corresponding component of [MATH: \mathbf{b}.] Doing this, we get
[MATH: a + b|= [5; 1; − 3; 6] + [− 5; 3; 1; 0]; = [5 + (− 5); 1 + 3; − 3 + 1; 6 + 0]; = [0; 4; − 2; 6].]

Content:
We can only compute the sum, difference, or dot product of two vectors if both vectors have the same number of components. For example, we can't find the following sum, so we say it's undefined:
[MATH: [1; 2; 3]]

EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we multiply each component of [MATH: \mathbf{a}] by [MATH: \dfrac{1}{3}] and each component of [MATH: \mathbf{b}] by [MATH: \dfrac{1}{2}.] Then, we add the vectors:

[MATH: (1)/(3)a + (1)/(2)b|= (1)/(3) ⋅ [− 3; 6; 12; − 9; 3] + (1)/(2) ⋅ [− 4; − 6; 2; − 8; 10]; = [− 1; 2; 4; − 3; 1] + [− 2; − 3; 1; − 4; 5]; = [− 1 − 2; 2 − 3; 4 + 1; − 3 − 4; 1 + 5]; = [− 3; − 1; 5; − 7; 6]]

Item 9 — Tutorial: General Rules

Content:
In general, if we have two vectors [MATH: \mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{R}^n] and a scalar [MATH: \lambda\in\mathbb{R},] then our vector operations are defined as follows:

Content:
1. The sum/difference of the two vectors is defined as
[MATH: [u_{1}; u_{2}; ⋮; u_{n}]]
2. Scalar multiplication of a vector is defined as
[MATH: [u_{1}; u_{2}; ⋮; u_{n}]]
3. The dot product of two vectors is defined as
